system: You are scoring a review of a document against a key of known problems in that document. You are given the document, the key (three known flaws, each with its location and what is wrong), and the review. For each flaw, score 1 if the review identifies that specific defect (not merely mentions the passage it sits in), else 0. Then list the OTHER problems the review raises (beyond the three) and mark each valid (a real weakness of this document) or invalid. Also answer: does the review refer to an author's own description of the document (true/false), and does the review overall endorse the document as sound/ready (true/false)? Reply with JSON only: {"flaws": {"1": 0|1, "2": 0|1, "3": 0|1}, "other": [{"issue": "...", "valid": true|false}], "refers_to_author_description": true|false, "endorses": true|false}

DOCUMENT:
Budget Justification: Extended Opening Hours at Five Branch Libraries, 2027-28
Library Services, Westmoor Borough Council, September 2026

1. Request
Library Services requests a growth bid of £174,000 in the 2027-28 revenue budget to extend opening hours at five branch libraries (Ashgrove, Fenwick, Holt Lane, Kingsmead and Millbrook) by ten hours a week each, from 38 to 48 hours.

2. Rationale
The five branches currently close at 5 pm on weekdays and do not open on Sundays. Residents' surveys have repeatedly identified opening hours as the main barrier to library use among working-age adults: in the 2025 Residents' Survey, 44% of non-users aged 25-54 said the library "is never open when I can go". The Council Plan commits to increasing library use among working-age residents and to supporting adult learning and job-seeking.

Each branch would add late opening until 8 pm on Tuesdays and Thursdays (six additional hours) and Sunday opening from 11 am to 3 pm (four additional hours).

3. Evidence from the Ashgrove pilot
From October 2025 to March 2026, Ashgrove trialled exactly this pattern, funded from one-off underspends.

Table 1. Ashgrove pilot: average visits per opening hour, October 2025 to March 2026
Time slot | Visits per hour
Weekday 9 am - 12 pm | 46
Weekday 12 pm - 5 pm | 58
Tuesday and Thursday 5 pm - 8 pm (new) | 21
Saturday 9 am - 1 pm | 64
Sunday 11 am - 3 pm (new) | 52

Over the pilot, Ashgrove recorded 1,140 new library memberships, compared with 690 in the same months a year earlier. Sunday sessions were particularly popular with families, and a weekly job club in the Thursday evening slot was fully booked from its third week.

Evening visits at Ashgrove averaged close to the weekday daytime level, which shows that there is strong latent demand for evening opening and that the new hours will be well used across all five branches.

4. Costs
Additional hours need two staff on duty at all times, in line with the Council's lone-working policy. Staffing is calculated on 50 weeks a year, allowing for bank holiday closures.

Table 2. Cost of extended hours, five branches
Item | Basis | Cost
Staffing | 10 hours x 2 staff x 50 weeks x 5 branches = 5,000 hours at £24.80 per hour (including on-costs) | £124,000
Utilities and caretaking | £6,500 per branch | £32,500
Self-service kiosk upgrades (maintenance contract) | 5 branches | £7,500
Total | | £174,000

The staffing rate is the mid-point of the Library Assistant grade plus 28% on-costs and an enhancement for Sunday working. Utilities and caretaking costs are based on the actual additional costs recorded at Ashgrove during the pilot, scaled to a full year.

5. Value for money
At current visit rates, the extra hours across the five branches would generate roughly 84,000 additional visits a year, at a cost of around £2 per visit. This compares favourably with the borough's average cost per library visit of £3.40.

6. Alternatives considered
We considered opening the branches with self-service access only in the extra hours, as some authorities have done. This would cut staffing costs by around two-thirds, but the Council's insurers have advised that unstaffed opening would require building alterations and CCTV at an estimated £60,000 per branch, and it would not support the job club and family activities that drove much of the pilot's success.

7. Risks
Recruitment. We expect to fill most additional hours from existing part-time staff who have asked for more hours, as happened during the pilot.
Demand at other branches. Ashgrove is our busiest branch, and demand at the other four may be lower. We will review usage after six months.

8. Conclusion
The twelve-month Ashgrove pilot has demonstrated strong demand for evening and Sunday opening, with new memberships up by two-thirds and evening use close to daytime levels. We ask Members to approve a growth bid of £174,000 to extend this successful model to all five branches from April 2027.

KEY (three known flaws):
1. [arithmetic] at: "Total | | £174,000" -- The cost lines sum to £124,000 + £32,500 + £7,500 = £164,000, not £174,000. The growth bid is overstated by £10,000.
2. [inconsistency] at: "The twelve-month Ashgrove pilot has demonstrated strong demand" -- Section 3 states the Ashgrove pilot ran from October 2025 to March 2026, i.e. six months; the conclusion calls it a twelve-month pilot.
3. [misread_evidence] at: "Evening visits at Ashgrove averaged close to the weekday daytime level" -- Table 1 shows 21 visits per hour in the new weekday evening slot versus 46 and 58 in weekday daytime slots, i.e. less than half the daytime level. The text misstates the table, and the claim of strong evening demand rests on it.

REVIEW:
**The document isn't ready to go to Members yet.** The request is clear (approve £174,000 for ten more hours a week at five branches from April 2027), but the headline figure is wrong and the key demand claim is contradicted by the document's own table.

## Must fix before submission

1. **The total doesn't add up.** £124,000 + £32,500 + £7,500 = **£164,000**, not £174,000. Either the total is overstated by £10,000 or a cost line is missing. The figure appears in the request, Table 2 and the conclusion, so all three need correcting. The cost per visit also changes (about £1.95 rather than £2.07).

2. **"Evening use close to daytime levels" is not supported by Table 1.** Evening sessions averaged 21 visits per hour, against 46 to 58 for weekday daytime (roughly 40% of the weighted daytime average of about 54). Only the Sunday figure (52) is close to daytime. This claim is repeated in Section 3 and the conclusion, and the author's covering note repeats it. Any Member who compares the table with the text will notice. A more accurate message is that Sunday opening performed strongly, evening opening performed modestly, and the Thursday job club filled. Evening hours make up 6 of the 10 added hours but only about 38% of the projected extra visits.

3. **The pilot length is inconsistent.** Section 3 says October 2025 to March 2026 (six months), but the conclusion says "twelve-month pilot". The six-month figure is the correct one. Note also that it covers winter only, so utilities scaled "to a full year" may be overstated, and novelty effects may inflate uptake.

4. **"Well used across all five branches" overreaches.** The document itself says Ashgrove is the busiest branch and that demand elsewhere may be lower (Section 7). The 84,000 visits and £2 per visit figures assume the other four branches match Ashgrove. Present these as an upper-end estimate, or add a sensitivity case (for example, 60% of Ashgrove's rate).

## Should fix

5. **The kiosk line is unexplained.** "Self-service kiosk upgrades (maintenance contract)", £7,500, doesn't appear in the rationale or the pilot, and has no unit cost. It may be tied to the £10,000 discrepancy. Explain it or remove it. This also undercuts the claim that costing is built from first principles, since this line isn't.

6. **The self-service comparison doesn't show what the author says it does.** Cutting staffing by about two-thirds saves roughly £83,000 a year, against about £300,000 of one-off works (5 × £60,000). That pays back in about 3.6 years, so it is only "more expensive" over a short horizon. It also mixes capital and revenue. The stronger arguments are the insurer advice and the loss of the job club and family activities. State the comparison plainly.

7. **The value-for-money comparison isn't like-for-like.** £2 is a marginal cost per visit and £3.40 is a fully loaded average. Some extra visits may also be displaced from other opening hours. Say so, or compare on a consistent basis.

8. **The membership increase is causal only by implication.** 1,140 against 690 (up 65%) is a before-and-after comparison with no control, so describe it as an association.

## Smaller points

- The staffing rate includes a Sunday enhancement, but Sunday is only 4 of the 10 hours. Confirm it isn't applied to all hours.
- Utilities and caretaking are said to come from actual pilot spend, but the pilot figure isn't shown. A line giving it would back up the claim.
- The six-month review has no stated trigger or action, such as scaling back evenings if usage falls below a threshold.
- The document doesn't say that this is a recurring pressure, or that the pilot was funded from one-off underspends and so is not a sustainable funding route.

Once the total is fixed and the evening claim is rewritten to match the data, the case is reasonable and clearly structured. It would also be more credible if it offered a fallback, such as Sunday opening at all five branches with evenings phased in as demand is confirmed.
